memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The sons of Jacob's wife Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin. In Egypt, Manasseh and Ephraim were born to Joseph by Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On... These were the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob—fourteen in all." — Gen 46:19-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Rachel is called "Jacob's wife" — the only one of the four mothers given that title here — and it is a quiet reminder of how deeply Jacob loved her. She died young, on the road, giving birth to Benjamin (Gen 35:19). She never saw any of this.

She never knew Joseph became a ruler. She never met her grandchildren. She died believing she had two small sons and nothing else settled.

And yet look what came from her line. Fourteen names recorded. Two tribes from Joseph alone — Ephraim and Manasseh — who would become among the largest in Israel.

Rachel's story is a comfort to everyone who dies before seeing how things turn out. Most of us will. We pray for children whose futures we will not see, plant things we will not harvest, and hand on faith whose fruit will appear long after we are gone.

Hebrews says of the patriarchs that they died without receiving the things promised, but saw them from a distance and welcomed them (Heb 11:13). Faith is not knowing how the story ends. It is trusting the One who is writing it.

Whatever you are sowing that you may never see grow — God sees the whole page.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you investing in whose outcome you may never see?
2. How does it help to know God's work continues beyond your lifetime?
3. Who prayed or laboured for you before you existed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I will not see how much of my life's work turns out. Help me sow faithfully and trust You with the harvest, whether or not I am there for it. Amen.
